entry.title: Warriors vs. Pelicans player grades: Dominance from Steph Curry, Yaxel Lendeborg, and Brandin Podziemski
entry.summary: Well that was fun. The Golden State Warriors made NBA history on Monday night, by becoming the first team to start 0-3 and follow it up with an eight-game winning streak. And they certainly did it in emphatic style, as they positively crushed the New Orleans Pelicans, ending their home-stand with a 138-87 victory that […]
entry.content:
Well that was fun. The Golden State Warriors made NBA history on Monday night, by becoming the first team to start 0-3 and follow it up with an eight-game winning streak. And they certainly did it in emphatic style, as they positively crushed the New Orleans Pelicans, ending their home-stand with a 138-87 victory that was every bit as lopsided as the score would suggest.

Needless to say, the grades are going to be good for this one. As always, my grades are based on my personal expectations for each player, with a “B” grade representing that player’s average performance.

Note: True-shooting percentage (TS) is a scoring efficiency metric that accounts for threes and free throws. Entering Monday’s games, league-average TS was 57.1%.

Gui Santos

21 minutes, 3 points, 7 rebounds, 4 assists, 1 block, 3 fouls, 0-for-3 shooting, 0-for-1 threes, 3-for-4 free throws, 31.5% TS, +21

You gotta love Gui. Even in a game where the Warriors were pouring in points faster than a bartender pours shots, Santos was content to just help out doing the little things. He attacked the glass and did a swell job of keeping the ball moving. He repeatedly found the open man and ended up with four dimes and zero turnovers. He was a big part of the strong defensive performance.

He just does all the little things, and even though it doesn’t always come with offense, you can happily live with that on this team.

Grade: B+

Yaxel Lendeborg

27 minutes, 23 points, 7 rebounds, 4 assists, 1 steal, 2 turnovers, 3 fouls, 8-for-10 shooting, 4-for-4 threes, 3-for-4 free throws, 97.8% TS, +34

Yeah. I think we have a star on our hands, friends. I don’t think Lendeborg is good, or even really good, or even has the potential to be a star. I think he is a star, point blank. It’s only been 11 games but that’s abundantly clear.

There was some Steph Curry in Yax’s game on Monday, in that he seemed to relish the opportunity to rip a team’s soul out. So often you see rookies get sloppy when playing in a blowout. At best they hog the ball and put on their own show; at worst, they check out because the outcome is determined.

But stars like Curry lock in. They want the win to be as lopsided as possible. They want to crush the other team’s spirit and make it clear that they’re not in the same league (except, you know … in the literal sense). And they want to make sure that they’re the one who does the damage.

Lendeborg, it seems, has that gene. He didn’t try to do to much, even when the Dubs led by 20, or 30, or 40, or 50. There were no reckless heat checks or audacious dunk attempts. Instead, he just locked in like it was a tied game, and went after the Pelicans in every part of the game.

And he dominated them in the process.

Grade: A+

Draymond Green

21 minutes, 2 points, 3 rebounds, 6 assists, 1 steal, 2 turnovers, 1 foul, 1-for-1 shooting, 100.0% TS, +32

Shot check! Green is up to 27 field goal attempts in nine games. There was some offseason chatter that Steve Kerr wanted Green to shoot more (specifically threes), and then it turned out the Warriors offense was good enough that Dray could be super selective, and focus on the three things he does brilliantly on that end of the court: passing the ball, setting screens, and making sure that everything runs through Curry.

Green has really been an offensive asset this year, which is a testament to his patience and playmaking, but also to the players around him. Having four shooters on the court at almost all times certainly helps there as well.

Defensively, Dray played well, though we were robbed of getting to see him defend Zion Williamson, as the Pelicans’ star got the night off. Oh well; they’ll meet again in a week.

Grade: A
Post-game bonus: Tied for the team lead in assists.

Brandin Podziemski

26 minutes, 25 points, 2 rebounds, 4 assists, 1 steal, 1 block, 10-for-19 shooting, 5-for-11 threes, 65.8% TS, +36

Lest you get too caught up in the Yaxel hype, Podziemski is here to remind you that there’s more than one early-20s Warrior with a fun European name who just might be a star. This was Podz at his very best. He was all over the court in a blur of chaos, on both ends of the court. He attacked on offense, while also popping out time and time again, and hiding behind screens, to show off his jumper … which looks a lot better this year (he’s 25-for-62 from deep so far this year).

In a fast and frantic game in which Podziemski seemed to have the ball in his hands a lot, he went a whole game with nary a turnover nor a foul.

It really feels like his offense is far more in control this year. He’s always had creativity and unique explosiveness, but this year he’s harnessed it far better than in year’s past. Can you remember a single shot he’s taken this season that has made you scratch your head or yell at the TV (except in a positive way)? I can’t. He’s just unbelievably in control, and fully coming into his own.

Grade: A+
Post-game bonus: Tied for the team lead in points; best plus/minus on the team.

Steph Curry

21 minutes, 25 points, 5 rebounds, 2 assists, 1 turnover, 6-for-10 shooting, 4-for-7 threes, 9-for-9 free throws, 89.5% TS, +32

Here’s a fun question: who’s enjoying the Lendeborg and Podziemski breakouts more, Curry or Kerr? Steph is clearly having the time of his life playing with these invigorating youngsters. And more importantly, you can see the relief in not having to carry the team on his shoulders night in and night out, and possession in and possession out.

The way that Curry is picking his spots is honestly a little reminiscent of when Klay Thompson and Kevin Durant were on the team. Curry knows he can step into his easier roles — playing the distributing point guard, or just using his gravity to space the defense out — and the offense will still function well. And then, when the time comes — if the team’s in trouble, or he wants to put a nail in the coffin, or he just wants to have a little fun — he goes into supersduperduperstar mode.

He’s averaging more than a point per minute with a true-shooting percentage well into the 70s. And it looks sustainable because he’s not having to kill himself out there. I should give him an A+ but i can’t justify a perfect grade for someone I know can — and will — pop off for 50.

Grade: A
Post-game bonus: Tied for the team lead in points.

De’Anthony Melton

26 minutes, 16 points, 4 rebounds, 3 assists, 1 steal, 1 turnover, 3 fouls, 5-for-11 shooting, 4-for-8 threes, 2-for-2 free throws, 67.3% TS, +20

Melton had a little bit of a slow start to the season, but new he is absolutely picking it up. He’s firing on all cylinders right now, and just making everything work. He has so much veteran savvy and poise … he plays with a little bit of that old man game where everything is slow, but then he displays these little bursts when they’re needed, to turn a rebound into a transition opportunity, or cut to the hoop, or strip a driving opponent. There’s more than a little bit of Andre Iguodala in his game, that’s for sure.

Like Curry, Melton has really been excelling at picking his spots this year, and that goes for both offense and defense. In this one, he came in with the bench unit and helped turn a solid lead into a blowout, and he never took his foot off the gas.

Grade: A

Al Horford

15 minutes, 5 points, 2 rebounds, 6 assists, 2 steals, 3 blocks, 2 fouls, 2-for-5 shooting, 1-for-3 threes, 50.0% TS, +29

I’m just so happy that Horford is on this team. What a treat he is to watch. He never seems to make a poor play or be out of position, and sometimes he just goes on little flurries, such as what he did at the start of the second quarter to help ensure that this game would stay a blowout. He had five stocks in 15 minutes. He had six assists — as a center — in 15 minutes. It’s just comical how frequently he makes the right play.

I said when the Warriors signed him before last year that he was the perfect player for Kerr, and I think that dramatically undersold it.

Grade: A+
Post-game bonus: Tied for the team lead in assists.

Georges Niang

19 minutes, 9 points, 2 rebounds, 2 assists, 1 block, 1 turnover, 4-for-7 shooting, 1-for-3 threes, 64.3% TS, +8

Just another quietly exceptional day at the office for Niang. He shows up, he stirs things up, he drains some threes, he makes some extra passes, he plays some defense, and he celebrates a win. Good life.

Grade: B

Brandon Williams

2 minutes, 4 points, 2-for-3 shooting, 66.7% TS, +4

Williams was only on the court for 99 seconds, but he changed the game in that brief time with the quickness with which he got down the court and attacked the basket. Unfortunately, he aggravated his hamstring in the first quarter, and was ruled out for the rest of the game. Hopefully he won’t be sidelined for too long.

Grade: P for Please get healthy soon
Post-game bonus: Tied for the worst plus/minus on the team.

Charles Bassey

18 minutes, 12 points, 10 rebounds, 1 assist, 1 block, 1 turnover, 2 fouls, 6-for-8 shooting, 75.0% TS, +18

With every passing game, Bassey makes it easier and easier to forget that Kristaps Porziņģis was supposed to be a part of this team. He only needed 18 minutes to nab a double-double and have one of the nastiest blocks you’ll see all season. We knew he had skills, but the way he’s able to fully control the paint — in terms of scoring, defending, and rebounding — is shocking.

Grade: A+

LJ Cryer

20 minutes, 10 points, 3 assists, 1 turnover, 1 foul, 4-for-9 shooting, 2-for-6 threes, 55.6% TS, +13

Cryer was forced into duty early on, after Williams’ injury. And he responded quite well. He scores in a different way than Williams does, but he sure can be a lightning rod as well. His jump shot is so slick, and I love the way he works into the defense, and then retreats … it reminds me a little bit of Jameer Nelson, or honestly, even Chris Paul.

This team is deep enough that Cryer is probably only going to get opportunities in situations like this, but it was great seeing him make the most of it.

Grade: B+

Graham Ike

12 minutes, 4 points, 5 rebounds, 2 assists, 1 block, 1 turnover, 2 fouls, 2-for-4 shooting, 0-for-1 threes, 50.0% TS, +4

Cryer got the most minutes of the two-way players in this game due to Williams’ injury, but Ike remains the two-way contract most capable of helping the team on a nightly basis. There aren’t many minutes for him now — he was limited to extended garbage time in this game — but you can see why Kerr is so excited to get him out there, and believes he can help. He does so many good things on the court.

Grade: A-
Post-game bonus: Tied for the worst plus/minus on the team.

Malevy Leons

12 minutes, 0 points, 3 rebounds, 1 block, 1 turnover, 1 foul, 0-for-1 shooting, 0.0% TS, +4

Nice to see Leons get some serious run. Like Ike, he played the entire fourth quarter since the Warriors were up by 47 points going into the final frame. He did some nice things out there.

Grade: B
Post-game bonus: Tied for the worst plus/minus on the team.

Monday’s inactives: Jimmy Butler III, Moses Moody, Gary Payton II, Kristaps Porziņģis, Will Richard

entry.title: Steph Curry, Warriors coast to 138-87 blowout victory over Pelicans
entry.summary: The Golden State Warriors dominated the New Orleans Pelicans on Monday night, coasting to a 138-87 victory. The Pelicans were playing the second half of a back-to-back and missing several key players, including Zion Williamson and Trey Murphy III. Nevertheless, the Warriors took care of business and improved to 8-3 on the season. They have […]
entry.content:
The Golden State Warriors dominated the New Orleans Pelicans on Monday night, coasting to a 138-87 victory. The Pelicans were playing the second half of a back-to-back and missing several key players, including Zion Williamson and Trey Murphy III. Nevertheless, the Warriors took care of business and improved to 8-3 on the season. They have now one eight consecutive games and went undefeated on their five-game homestand.

It truly took no time for the Warriors to get rolling. Steph Curry quickly found plenty of open space against the Pelicans defense. On the other end, New Orleans looked sluggish and simply lacked the firepower to generate any run of their own. Golden State led 35-20 by the end of the first quarter.

While the on-court results were fantastic for the Warriors, they did lose backup guard Brandon Williams who only played a couple of minutes before leaving the game with a left hamstring injury. He will undergo an MRI tomorrow. If Williams has to miss extended time, he would join Jimmy Butler, Moses Moody, and Kristaps Porzingis as Warriors who will be out for awhile. Will Richard could also be on that list soon if he undergoes surgery on his torn UCL in his left thumb. Gary Payton II was also ruled out with knee inflammation for Monday night’s game, although that is not expected to lead to a prolonged absence.

Two-way guard LJ Cryer got plenty of minutes in Williams’ place. Charles Bassey perhaps had the highlight of the night, blocking Derik Queen on a two-handed dunk attempt. Brandin Podziemski got the ball in transition and made a three on the other end. Queen, by the way, led the Pelicans with 16 points in the game.

By halftime, the Warriors led 72-43 with rookie Yaxel Lendeborg leading the team in scoring with 16 points on just 6 field-goal attempts (4-for-4 from three). Podziemski was right behind him with 15 points of his own. By the end of regulation, Lendeborg recorded 23 points, 7 rebounds, 4 assists, 1 steal, and 2 turnovers while shooting 8-for-10 from the field. Podz finished tied for a game-high 25 points.

Curry carried the offensive load in the third quarter, finishing the game with 25 points, 5 rebounds, and 2 assists on 6-for-10 shooting from the field in under 21 minutes of action. De’Anthony Melton (16 points), Bassey (12), and Cryer (10) were the only other Warriors in double figures. However, 12 of the 13 Dubs who appeared in the game made at least one basket.

The Warriors will now head on the team’s first prolonged road trip of the season. While they have done an impressive job climbing the standings after an 0-3 start, Golden State’s schedule is about to get a lot more difficult. They will get the trip started on Wednesday when they face the Houston Rockets. Opening tip is scheduled for 6:30 p.m. Pacific Time.

entry.title: Brandon Williams leaves Warriors game with hamstring injury
entry.summary: The Golden State Warriors are positively cruising, despite dealing with a lot of injuries. Jimmy Butler III and Moses Moody have yet to play this season, and are still a few months away, while Kristaps Porziņģis is stepping away from the sport. Gui Santos and Gary Payton II have struggled with injuries in the opening […]
entry.content:
The Golden State Warriors are positively cruising, despite dealing with a lot of injuries. Jimmy Butler III and Moses Moody have yet to play this season, and are still a few months away, while Kristaps Porziņģis is stepping away from the sport. Gui Santos and Gary Payton II have struggled with injuries in the opening weeks, and Will Richard is sidelined with a UCL tear in his thumb.

And unfortunately, those injuries took a hit on Monday, during the Warriors’ home game over the New Orleans Pelicans, as reserve guard Brandon Williams left the game with a hamstring injury and has been ruled out for the rest of the contest. As usual, Williams entered the game in the first quarter, and immediately provided a spark with an instant burst of super-speedy offense. But his initial stint on the court was short lived, and when the second quarter arrived, it was two-way contract LJ Cryer on the court rather than Williams.

In the third quarter, the Warriors officially ruled Williams out for the rest of the game with a left hamstring injury. Hopefully it’s minor, and won’t cost the electric guard much time.

entry.title: Warriors won’t give up picks for Myles Turner
entry.summary: The Golden State Warriors would like to trade Kristaps Porzingis by December 15. However, they’re not about to sacrifice draft capital to do it for a long-term contract. There’s not a ton of pressure on the Warriors to trade Porzingis, who isn’t being paid as he decides to “step away” from basketball, which he allegedly […]
entry.content:
The Golden State Warriors would like to trade Kristaps Porzingis by December 15. However, they’re not about to sacrifice draft capital to do it for a long-term contract.

There’s not a ton of pressure on the Warriors to trade Porzingis, who isn’t being paid as he decides to “step away” from basketball, which he allegedly loves. He and the NBA Players Association aren’t planning to challenge to Warriors taking him off the payroll, which saves Joe Lacob about $250K per game. He may not play this season, for the Warriors or anyone else, but that doesn’t mean his contract is an albatross.

According to Clutch Points, the Warriors have had trade talks regarding Porzingis with the Chicago Bulls, New Orleans Pelicans, and Milwaukee Bucks. They’re reportedly interested in 26-year-old center Jalen Smith of the Bulls, who is making $9.4M in the last year of his contract. It’s not clear who on the Pelicans’ roster has interested the Warriors, but with the Bucks, it’s center Myles Turner, who is signed through 2029 for $82.6M.

The Bucks want the Warriors to give them draft picks in a Turner trade, which would have to include another player (Moses Moody?) heading to Milwaukee, as the Warriors can’t take back more money than they send out. The Warriors think that taking on that much of Turner’s salary means they should be getting a draft pick, not the Bucks.

Turner is having a wretched season for the Bucks, who are in a weird rebuild limbo since trading Giannis Antetokounmpo this summer. They got four players back from the Miami Heat, drafted two players in the lottery, and have veterans Tyler Herro, Kyle Kuzma, and Caris Levert on expiring deals. They’re 1-9 and since they don’t have their own first-round pick until 2031, the Bucks don’t even have incentive to avoid the lottery penalty for having one of the league’s worst records.

The 30-year-old Turner is averaging 7.1 points and 5.7 rebounds this season, though he is blocking 2.5 shots per game. His effort seems to be lacking, as seen in a blowout loss to the Boston Celtics Sunday.

What Turner can provide, assuming he’s trying, is a rare combination of rim protection and outside shooting. He’s a career 36.4% three-point shooter and has blocked 2.1 shots per game for his career. Turner was the pivot man on an Indiana Pacers team that was a Tyrese Haliburton Achilles injury from winning a title. It’s easy to see how he’s a logical replacement for Porzingis, with the bonus that he’s played at least 71 games the last three seasons.

But his contract is n0t good. It’s even worse for the Bucks, since they waived-and-stretched Damian Lillard’s contract to afford the deal, and Dame Time now costs them $22.5M on the salary cap for each of the next four seasons. By contrast, Porzingis is on the books for only $3M next season, isn’t get paid anything right now, and might take a buyout on the $17M+ remaining on this year’s deal.

The key calendar date for the Warriors is Dec. 15, because of the NBA’s “reaggregation” rule. Players acquired before that date can be combined with other players/contracts until the trade deadline. This came up for the Warriors in Dec. 2024, when they traded De’Anthony Melton for Dennis Schroder just before the reaggregation deadline, then aggregated Schroder’s salary in the blockbuster trade for Jimmy Butler.

That’s why a player like Smith could be more appealing for the Warriors than Smith, as he could provide temporary help while still remaining highly moveable in a later trade. The Warriors could conceivably take back their old friend Buddy Hield in such a trade, as his salary and Smith’s are still less than Porzingis’ total money — and Hield can be waived next summer for just over $3M.

There’s a lot of possibilities for what the Warriors do with Porzingis. But giving up future draft picks to ditch him does not seem to be one of them.

entry.title: Warriors vs. Pelicans injury report: No Zion Williamson or Trey Murphy III
entry.summary: The Golden State Warriors are looking to win their eighth straight game — and sweep the home stand — when they take on old friend Jordan Poole and the New Orleans Pelicans tonight at the Chase Center. Both teams will have their depth chart tested, as the list of ailments is long and notable. Here’s […]
entry.content:
The Golden State Warriors are looking to win their eighth straight game — and sweep the home stand — when they take on old friend Jordan Poole and the New Orleans Pelicans tonight at the Chase Center. Both teams will have their depth chart tested, as the list of ailments is long and notable.

Here’s the full injury report for both teams.

Warriors

Out — Will Richard (left thumb UCL tear)

Really tough news for Richard on Sunday. The second-year guard, who had a brilliant week of play and is really settling into his own, was revealed to have a UCL tear in his non-shooting thumb, which could cost him a few weeks or even a few months.

Out — Gary Payton II (left knee inflammation)

With both Richard and Payton out, the Warriors perimeter defense is going to be severely compromised tonight. Fortunately, they’re facing a below-average Pelicans offense which is also missing some key players.

Out — Jimmy Butler III (right ACL repair surgery)
Out — Moses Moody (left patellar tendon repair surgery)
Out — Kristaps Porziņģis (not with team)

The standard trio. Butler is progressing nicely, but these three will likely be a staple of this section of the injury report until Porziņģis is traded.

Available — Gui Santos (left knee tendinitis)

Hey, some good news! Santos is still dealing with some knee pain, but thankfully is able to play.

Pelicans

Out — Zion Williamson (rest)

Williamson has battled health issues his entire career, so it’s not surprising to see him get a rest day, especially since the Pelicans played (and traveled) last night. It’s great seeing him healthy, though, as he’s appeared in all 10 games prior to this one, and is averaging 33 minutes per night.

Out — Trey Murphy III (bilateral patellar tendinopathy)

We know the Warriors have had their sights set on a Murphy trade for a while. Unfortunately for their scouts — but fortunately for their prospects of winning tonight — they won’t get to see him in this game.

Out — Yves Missi (left knee contusion/bone bruise)

The Dubs have also been linked to Missi, as a potential target to replace the retiring Porziņģis. The third-year center was injured in the second game of the season, and hasn’t played since.

Out — Trendon Watford (right ankle sprain)

Watford has been a solid bench contributor in his first season in the bayou, so NOLA’s bench will be shortened by his absence tonight.

Enjoy the game, Dub Nation. It tips off at 7:00 p.m. PT on NBA TV and NBC Sports Bay Area.

entry.title: Will Jordan Poole play vs Warriors as Pelicans come to Chase?
entry.summary: The Golden State Warriors wrap up their six-game homestand tonight against the New Orleans Pelicans, which means Jordan Poole is back at Chase Center wearing a New Orleans jersey and, if the last week is any indication, a warmup top he might never take off. He isn’t on the Pelicans’ injury report. He just sat […]
entry.content:
The Golden State Warriors wrap up their six-game homestand tonight against the New Orleans Pelicans, which means Jordan Poole is back at Chase Center wearing a New Orleans jersey and, if the last week is any indication, a warmup top he might never take off. He isn’t on the Pelicans’ injury report. He just sat the entire game in Los Angeles on Sunday with a coach’s decision DNP, and he’s played four games all season, averaging six points on 19 percent shooting.

Remember when Poole, James Wiseman and Jonathan Kuminga were supposed to be the Warriors’ future? The two-timelines plan had them growing up next to Steph Curry and Draymond Green and eventually taking the keys. All three are gone. Wiseman is getting about five minutes a night as a backup center in New York. Kuminga is starting in Minnesota and scoring 12.3 points per game. Poole is in the final year of the $123 million extension Golden State gave him, watching from the end of the Pelicans’ bench.

Which is wild, because Poole is a big reason there’s a 2022 banner hanging in this building. He scored 17 a night in that playoff run, and Steve Kerr mentioned it plainly when Poole came back with Washington: “We don’t win that championship without him,” he told ESPN.

But that was then, and this is YAXEL. Right now this fan base is losing its mind over a 6-foot-9 rookie who plays like nobody told him he’s a rookie. Yaxel Lendeborg is pulling up off the dribble, crashing the glass and leading fast breaks, and on Nov. 1 he dropped 37 on the Clippers at Chase Center with Curry resting, the most by a Warriors rookie since Curry scored 42 in 2010. Nine games in, the No. 11 pick is at 21.0 points and 7.1 rebounds a night.

Now rewind to May 14, 2021. Curry sat that night too, and a third-year Poole scored a then-career-high 38 against New Orleans at Chase Center. Something about Curry being out can provide opportunities for young players to showcase their abilities.

And yes, Yaxel went to Michigan, too. Poole helped the Wolverines reach the 2018 national title game, and Yaxel helped them win the 2026 one. I keep picturing Draymond Green, Michigan State Spartan to his bones, watching the Warriors crown a second Wolverine as the future in five years and quietly wondering who in the front office keeps a maize-and-blue flag in their desk drawer. And Poole knows first hand how about the Spartan gives tough love lessons.

Before anybody hands Yaxel the keys, though, Brandin Podziemski would like a word. Last month the Warriors gave him a five-year, $110 million extension, and he has never been shy about where he sees this going. “When they leave this thing, they got to leave it with somebody,” he told The Athletic last year, talking about Curry and Green trusting him with the franchise. Draymond’s advice at the time was to be careful saying that stuff out loud.

I wonder what Poole thought when he heard about a young Warriors guard with a fresh nine-figure extension talking about inheriting the franchise. He’s been there.

Moses Moody, the one young player from that “two timelines” era still on the roster, is working his way back from patellar tendon surgery and isn’t expected back until at least December, which gives Kerr one more young body to sort out when he does.

As for tonight, the Warriors have won seven straight after an 0-3 start, the first team to pull that off since the 1950-51 Boston Celtics. Curry is coming off 41 points in Saturday’s overtime win over Orlando, at 38 years old. The Pelicans are 4-6 and on the second night of a back-to-back after losing 139-123 to the Clippers, and New Orleans is without Yves Missi. Golden State will be without Jimmy Butler, Moody, Will Richard and Kristaps Porzingis, with Gui Santos probable, per the official injury report. Tip is at 7 p.m.

entry.title: Warriors guard Will Richard out indefinitely with ligament tear in thumb
entry.summary: The Golden State Warriors announced some surprising news on the team’s injury report for Monday night’s game against the New Orleans Pelicans. Per the Dubs official release, second-year guard Will Richard is out indefinitely with a torn ulnar collateral ligament (UCL) in his left thumb. A 2023 study found that NBA players who suffered in-season […]
entry.content:
The Golden State Warriors announced some surprising news on the team’s injury report for Monday night’s game against the New Orleans Pelicans. Per the Dubs official release, second-year guard Will Richard is out indefinitely with a torn ulnar collateral ligament (UCL) in his left thumb. A 2023 study found that NBA players who suffered in-season thumb UCL tears and underwent surgery missed on average 7.4 weeks of action (although there was a wide range of outcomes). Kings forward Keegan Murray suffered a similar injury last year and missed the first 15 games of the season.

The team has not ruled out Richard potentially wearing a splint and playing through the injury. However, they are waiting to see how the finger responds over the next few days before making that decision.

Whether Richard is out for a month, three, or more, head coach Steve Kerr will now have a fourth player on the roster unavailable to him in the rotation. Richard joins Jimmy Butler, Moses Moody, and Kristaps Porzingis on the Warriors list of players with prolonged absences. Richard was off to a promising start to his sophomore NBA season prior to the injury, averaging 5.1 points and 1.8 rebounds on 47.5%/42.9%/80.0% shooting in 17.2 minutes per game across 10 games (3 starts).

The Warriors acquired Richard on a draft night trade back in 2025, acquiring his rights via the 56th overall pick. Richard had helped Florida win a National Championship in his final collegiate season and quickly made an impression in Golden State, looking like an early steal. Richard exploded for 30 points in his seventh NBA game and quickly became a mainstay in the rotation. However, he never again reached those heights and became a solid role player whose effectiveness ebbed and flowed with his jump shot.

Thus far this season, Richard was making his threes, but he was also continuing to show veteran savvy as a backcutter in the Warriors offense. Moreover, he was one of Kerr’s go-to point of attack defenders against quick guards. Golden State already lacked point of attack defense, and the current roster does not have any obvious replacements for that component of Richard’s role. Gary Payton II will likely receive more opportunities with perhaps a few minutes for two-way wing Malevy Leons.

entry.title: How to watch Warriors vs. Pelicans
entry.summary: The Golden State Warriors will conclude their six-game homestand with Monday night’s matchup against the New Orleans Pelicans. Tip-off is scheduled for 7:00 PM PT in San Francisco and can be watched on NBA TV and NBC Sports Bay Area. Previously with the Warriors: Warriors fans were treated to another vintage performance from Stephen Curry […]
entry.content:
The Golden State Warriors will conclude their six-game homestand with Monday night’s matchup against the New Orleans Pelicans. Tip-off is scheduled for 7:00 PM PT in San Francisco and can be watched on NBA TV and NBC Sports Bay Area.

Previously with the Warriors:

Warriors fans were treated to another vintage performance from Stephen Curry on Saturday night. The 38-year-old superstar scored 41 points on 13-of-19 shooting from the field as he led Golden State to a 126-119 overtime victory against the Orlando Magic. Curry was especially brilliant down the stretch, scoring 17 points in the final seven minutes of regulation and overtime, as he carried the Warriors to their seventh win in a row.

What to watch for tonight:

After starting the season 0-3, the Warriors have flipped the script with seven consecutive wins, improving their record to 7-3. Much of that success has come during their current six-game homestand, which Golden State now has an opportunity to sweep with a win over the Pelicans on Monday night.

However, in order to do that, one area the Warriors will need to clean up is their work on the glass. Despite Saturday’s victory over Orlando, Golden State struggled to control the glass, particularly on second-chance opportunities, as the Magic held a staggering 24-3 advantage in offensive rebounds.

With the Pelicans’ 43.5 rebounds per game ranking just behind the Warriors (43.7), Monday’s matchup should present an opportunity for the Dubs to address their shortcomings on that end, especially with New Orleans playing without stars Zion Williamson and Trey Murphy.

Enjoy the game Dub Nation. GO WARRIORS!!!

Projected Starters

Warriors: Stephen Curry, Brandin Podziemski, Yaxel Lendeborg, Gui Santos, Draymond Green

Pelicans: Dejounte Murray, Jeremiah Fears, Saddiq Bey, Herbert Jones, Karlo Matkovic

Terry will likely go unclaimed on waivers and return to free agency less than a week after he first signed with Oklahoma City. Terry was […]
entry.content:
The Oklahoma City Thunder waived wing Dalen Terry on Sunday after acquiring a different wing (Niq Clifford) in a trade from the Sacramento Kings for a couple of second-round picks. Terry will likely go unclaimed on waivers and return to free agency less than a week after he first signed with Oklahoma City. Terry was slated to be the centerpiece of the Santa Cruz Warriors (the Golden State Warriors G-League affiliate). It’s worth wondering if he will return to Santa Cruz if he goes unclaimed.

Terry appeared in two games with the Thunder, recording 2 points, 6 rebounds, 1 assist, 1 steal, and 2 turnovers in 11 minutes. Terry’s deal with OKC was fully non-guaranteed so he will only receive a small pro-rated portion of the league minimum.

The Chicago Bulls drafted Terry with the 18th overall pick back in the 2022 NBA Draft out of Arizona. He appeared in 218 games over his first four seasons, but was unable to show enough potential to convince a team to dedicate a rotation spot for him heading into this season. The Bulls had declined Terry’s fifth-year option, and dealt him to the 76ers at last year’s deadline. After failing to get an NBA deal in free agency, he joined the Warriors a series of deals over the summer.

A 6’6 wing who just turned 24, Terry remains an intriguing 3-and-D prospect. The fact that an organization as renowned for scouting and development as the Thunder was willing to give him a trial window further endorses that side of things. Nevertheless, he has averaged just 3.5 points, 1.7 rebounds, and 1.2 assists on 44.3%/31.4%/63.8% shooting in 11.2 minutes per game over his career.

entry.title: Charles Bassey’s play is turning heads in Golden State

entry.content:
Every season I activate this trope to try and inspire a wary Dub Nation who wonders why we don’t replace (insert suspect player) with someone else in the league. You’re in the back seat of your mom’s car, those sweet sweet Golden Arches come into view, and you make your pitch: “Mom, can we PLEAAASEEE get McDonald’s?”

And without missing a beat, back comes the dreamcrushing sentence masquerading as a better suggestion: “We got McDonald’s at home.”

What’s at home is never McDonald’s, but it’s ground beef, sandwich bread, ketchup, mustard, and relish. You eat it and more often than not depending on who your mama is, it hits. Your tastebuds are awash with flavor and gratitude. Maybe mom was right, maybe you do have McDonalds at home.

That’s Charles Bassey for the Warriors right now. When Golden State asked for a real center, the front office looked at the cap sheet and injury report, and said, “we got a center at home.”

And maybe the Warriors front office is right, maybe we DO have a big man at home!

And that is quite the development considering the hope of Kristaps Porziņģis dominating as the big man for the Warriors has effectively died as it looks like he’s retiring from Warriors basketball. The team re-signed him this summer even though he’d missed 90 games over the past two seasons with three different teams.

Then there’s Al Horford, who is 40 years old and dealing with a body banged up from years of playoff warfare. Horford is a professional basketball genius. But asking him to play 30 minutes a night in November is not gonna have him available for any kinda playoff run in the spring.

And of course the Warriors can always counter with the grizzled, undersized legend Draymond Green at center. That works until Draymond does Draymond things and gets ejected two minutes into the third quarter, which brings us to the night the center at home showed up.

On Nov. 2 against the Suns, Golden State trailed by 17. Draymond had been thrown out for body slamming one Phoenix player and quasi strangling Dillon Brooks (rightfully so).

That’s when Bassey had a career night, scoring 19 points on 7-of-10 shooting, grabbed 8 rebounds and finished +10. After Draymond’s ejection, the Warriors outscored Phoenix 59-45. He also built a connection with rookie Yaxel Lendeborg. Four of Lendeborg’s five assists that night went to Bassey. Every time the rookie lofted the ball near the rim, Bassey caught it and finished.

After the game, Bassey called out the Suns for “fake toughness.” The center at home has a little seasoning on him, don’t he?

This wasn’t a one-night fluke. The Warriors started 0-3, then won seven straight to get to 7-3, and Bassey was in the middle of it:

  • He has a +34 plus-minus over the seven-game streak, and +33 in the five games where he played real minutes
  • His 15.7 rebounds per 36 minutes ranks second in the NBA
  • He’s shooting 63.6% from the field and 88.2% from the line, with a 25.8 PER.
  • Over the streak he’s averaging roughly 21 points, 15 rebounds and nearly 3 blocks per 36 minutes.

Ummm ladies and gentlemen, he’s really balling in his role right now. Here’s the case for more Bassey minutes: in the Orlando game, he played only 11. The Magic won the offensive rebounding battle 24-3 and outscored Golden State 33-2 on second-chance points. The Warriors still won in overtime, because Steph Curry is a supernatural force of nature on the basketball court.

Bassey isn’t Porziņģis, a guy who stretches the floor to 28 feet or make anyone’s All-Star ballot. He’s 6-foot-9 and focused completely on rebounding, rim-running and blocked shots. He’s also available to play, and we all know the best ability is availability.

Warriors GM Mike Dunleavy may still trade for a center; I absolutely think he should. Using Porziņģis’ contract to match salaries for a real big makes sense, and they have a real chance to pull it off before the trade deadline.

Until then, Dub Nation asked for McDonald’s and got told they had a center at home, and so far the one at home is providing a lot of sustenance.
